limitations: Only full directed de Bruijn graphs; not arbitrary primitive digraphs, asynchronous dynamics, or stochastic update rules.
The Poisson two-point law refers to binary word-length dimensions d=2^h+h+c and fair independent initial bits.
Historical equivalence in unindexed literature is not ruled out; a plausible de Bruijn broadcasting article was accessible only as an abstract.

The 1946 de Bruijn source is verified at year resolution only, so the 2008-05-02 date refers to the earliest checked original day-dated primary Boolean-network source, not an invented day for older literature.
scope: Synchronous Boolean OR of incoming neighbours on full directed de Bruijn graphs, with alphabet size at least two and word length at least one; an exact temporal census and a dimension-indexed initial-data cutoff.
title: A Poisson cutoff in exact OR consensus clocks on de Bruijn networks
